description: Extend the dashboard Balance screen with two sibling lenses — Intake and Expenditure — selectable via a 3-way segmented toggle. Presentation-only: DailyBalance already carries intake, burn, balance, bmr, tef, neat, eat, proteinG, carbG, fatG. Reuses existing chart + history-card styling. No data-layer, repository, or schema changes.

userStories.title: 3-way segmented toggle + view-mode state
userStories.description: As a user, I want a Balance | Intake | Expenditure toggle at the top of the Balance screen so I can switch lenses in one tap.
acceptanceCriteria: Add enum DashboardViewMode { BALANCE, INTAKE, EXPENDITURE } in ui/dashboard (new small file or alongside DashboardScreen).
Add a segmented-toggle composable rendered inside DashboardContent, below the date navigator and above the summary card.
Toggle state hoisted in DashboardContent via remember { mutableStateOf(DashboardViewMode.BALANCE) }; default BALANCE.
Selected segment uses MiOrange accent; unselected uses MiTextSecondary; matches existing rounded-pill styling (RoundedCornerShape(16.dp) background like the date navigator).
With BALANCE selected the screen renders identically to current behavior — no visual regression.

userStories.title: Chart plots the active view's value
userStories.description: As a user, I want the chart to reflect the lens I picked so the bars match the breakdown below.
acceptanceCriteria: Parameterize CalorieBalanceChart with a value selector ((DailyBalance) -> Double) plus a diverging/positive-only flag; do not duplicate the chart.
BALANCE mode unchanged: diverging bars around the zero line keyed on balance (positive MiOrange, negative tertiary).
INTAKE mode: plots intake per day as upward-only bars (no negative half).
EXPENDITURE mode: plots burn per day as upward-only bars.
Bar-height normalization for intake/expenditure uses the window max of the plotted value, not the balance max.
Day-initial labels and click-to-open-BreakdownDialog behavior preserved in all three modes.
DashboardContent passes the active DashboardViewMode into the chart.

compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64 passes

userStories.title: Summary insight card adapts per view
userStories.description: As a user, I want the big number and footer on the summary card to describe the lens I'm viewing.
acceptanceCriteria: BALANCE unchanged: 'AVERAGE BALANCE', trend chip, 'Total Week' / 'Trend' footer.
INTAKE: headline label 'AVERAGE INTAKE', value = mean of intake over the window in kcal; footer total = sum of intake.
EXPENDITURE: headline label 'AVERAGE EXPENDITURE', value = mean of burn; footer total = sum of burn.
Reuses existing formatCalorieValue and the card's typography/spacing; no new card style.
For INTAKE/EXPENDITURE the trend chip is hidden (do not show a green/red balance arrow that would mislead).

userStories.title: Intake history rows — macro grams + total kcal-in
userStories.description: As a user, in Intake view I want each day's history row to show carbs/protein/fat in grams and the day's total calories in.
acceptanceCriteria: History list reuses CondensedLogItem format/style, reverse-chronological (balances.reversed()), same Card with HorizontalDivider between rows.
Left column unchanged: day abbreviation + day-of-month number.
Middle: three rows Carbs / Protein / Fat, each with a colored dot (ColorCarbs / ColorProtein / ColorFat) and value in grams (e.g. '120g carbs') from carbG / proteinG / fatG rounded to whole grams.
Right: total kcal-in = intake.roundToInt() + ' kcal', styled like the existing right-side value; no +/- sign, not green/red.
Tapping a row still opens the existing BreakdownDialog (unchanged).
Parameterize CondensedLogItem per DashboardViewMode rather than forking the row.

userStories.title: Expenditure history rows — BMR/TEF/Active + total kcal-out
userStories.description: As a user, in Expenditure view I want each day's history row to show BMR / TEF / Active energy and the day's total calories out.
acceptanceCriteria: Same reused CondensedLogItem layout, reverse-chronological, same Card/divider styling.
Middle: three rows BMR / TEF / Active, each with a colored dot and a kcal value: bmr, tef, and Active = neat + eat, each rounded to whole kcal.
Dot colors match the burn-breakdown coloring used in BreakdownDialog: BMR = ColorProtein, TEF = ColorCarbs, Active = ColorFat.
Right: total kcal-out = burn.roundToInt() + ' kcal', styled like the existing right-side value; no sign, not green/red.
Sanity: bmr + tef + neat + eat equals burn (no fabricated reconciliation field if rounding drifts).
Tapping a row opens the existing BreakdownDialog (unchanged).
